analyst_view.overall: Early view: both sides come straight from Europe, with Celta hosting Bournemouth in the Europa League on Thursday 26 November and Villarreal away at Slavia Prague the night before. Celta's games are the lowest-scoring in the league (10 scored, 10 conceded in 12), Giráldez admits the team is tired and nervous in front of goal, and his injury list is long; Iñigo Pérez's Villarreal ended a poor run by beating Getafe 2-0 with 72% of the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Celta have scored and conceded 10 each in 12 games, two of their last three ended 0-0, and they had 23 shots and no goal against Levante, which Giráldez put down to nerves in the box. With both teams coming off European games, I lean lower, around 2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Villarreal's last three league games produced 13, 10 and 15 corners as Iñigo Pérez's side pin teams back, and Celta's home pressure against Levante brought 6 corners of their own. I lean higher, around 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Celta are a low-foul side (8 fouls and one yellow against Levante), and Renato Veiga is one booking away from a ban rather than suspended, as is Celta's Yoel Lago, which tends to make defenders careful. I lean slightly lower, around 3-4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots. Celta took 23 at home to Levante and Villarreal 22 against Getafe, so volume is there, but both teams will be on tired legs after midweek Europe. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Celta got 8 of their 23 shots on target against Levante and Villarreal 7 of 22 against Getafe; Borja Iglesias may only just be back from his calf injury, so I see no reason to move off the number.
